name: org-lsp
description: Org mode support through the org-lsp language server: highlighting, folding, outline, TODO states and the agenda.

org-lsp.server.path.markdownDescription: Path to the `org-lsp` server binary. When empty, the binary bundled with the extension is used, or else `org-lsp` from `PATH`.

org-lsp.conceal.markdownDescription: Hide what Org hides: link brackets and targets (`linkDescriptive`), and emphasis markers with `hideEmphasisMarkers`. It shows on the lines with a cursor.

enumDescriptions: In an editor group below the current one.
In an editor group beside the current one.
In a window of its own.
org-lsp.winSplitMode.markdownDescription: Where the agenda and capture buffers open.

org-lsp.settings.markdownDescription: The server's options, for example `{ "agendaFiles": ["~/org"], "todoKeywords": ["TODO", "NEXT", "|", "DONE"], "logDone": "time" }`. Without `agendaFiles`, the agenda is built from the Org files in the workspace folders. The options and their defaults are listed in [docs/vscode/configuration.md](https://github.com/kristijanhusak/org-lsp/blob/main/docs/vscode/configuration.md).

configFile.markdownDescription: The shared configuration file, whose options this editor's go on top of: `false` for none, or the path of another file (JSON if it ends in `.json`, else TOML). Unset, it is `$ORG_LSP_CONFIG`, else `config.toml` or `config.json` in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/org-lsp` (`~/.config/org-lsp`; `%APPDATA%\org-lsp` on Windows).

agendaFiles.markdownDescription: Files, directories and glob patterns (`*`, `?`, `**`) the agenda is built from. `~/` is the home directory, and a directory stands for the Org files directly in it. When empty, the agenda is built from the Org files under the workspace folders (hidden directories, `node_modules` and `target` left out), or else from the Org files that are open. (`org-agenda-files`)

todoKeywords.markdownDescription: The TODO sequence, written like Org's `#+TODO:` line. `|` separates the states that count as done; without it the last keyword is the only done state. `TODO(t)` gives a keyword a key for fast selection, and `WAIT(w@/!)` makes it log a note (`@`) or the time (`!`) on entering and leaving it. A file's own `#+TODO:` lines take precedence. (`org-todo-keywords`)

logDone.markdownDescription: Write `CLOSED:` with the time when an entry is done, and with `note` ask for a note too. (`org-log-done`)

logRepeat.markdownDescription: Record when a repeating entry is done and moves to its next date. (`org-log-repeat`)

logIntoDrawer.markdownDescription: Put state changes and notes into a drawer: `true` for `LOGBOOK`, or the name of a drawer. (`org-log-into-drawer`)

tagsColumn.markdownDescription: Where tags are aligned after a change to a headline. Negative: they end at that column. (`org-tags-column`)

clockIntoDrawer.markdownDescription: Where `CLOCK:` lines go: `true` for the drawer of `logIntoDrawer` (`LOGBOOK` when that is not a name), the name of a drawer, or `false` for the entry itself. (`org-clock-into-drawer`)

clockOutRemoveZeroTimeClocks.markdownDescription: Clocking out after less than a minute removes the `CLOCK:` line. (`org-clock-out-remove-zero-time-clocks`)

clockOutWhenDone.markdownDescription: Marking the clocked entry done stops the clock. (`org-clock-out-when-done`)

completeTagsAlwaysOfferAllAgendaTags.markdownDescription: Completing a tag offers the tags of every agenda file, after those of the file. Off, only the file's own. (`org-complete-tags-always-offer-all-agenda-tags`)

todoRepeatToState.markdownDescription: The state a repeating entry returns to when it is done: a keyword, or `true` for the state it had. (`org-todo-repeat-to-state`)

priorityDefault.markdownDescription: The priority of an entry without a cookie. A file's `#+PRIORITIES:` line takes precedence over the three priority options. (`org-priority-default`)

priorityStartCycleWithDefault.markdownDescription: Raising or lowering the priority of an entry that has none starts at the default. (`org-priority-start-cycle-with-default`)

timestampRoundingMinutes.markdownDescription: The step in which the minutes of a timestamp change (the second number of Org's option). (`org-time-stamp-rounding-minutes`)

readDatePreferFuture.markdownDescription: A date typed without a year or month is the next one to come. With `time`, a time that has passed today is tomorrow's. (`org-read-date-prefer-future`)

readDateForceCompatibleDates.markdownDescription: A typed year is kept within 1970 to 2037. (`org-read-date-force-compatible-dates`)

files.description: `current` (the entry's own file), `agenda`, a path or a list of paths

maxLevel.description: The headlines up to this level

regexp.description: The headlines that match this regular expression

todo.description: The headlines with this TODO keyword

refileTargets.markdownDescription: Where entries can be refiled to. Each entry has `files`: `current` (the entry's own file), `agenda`, a path or a list of paths; and one of `level`, `maxLevel`, `tag`, `todo`, `regexp` (the Rust `regex` crate's syntax) or `all` (true), which says which headlines there are targets. (`org-refile-targets`)

refileUseOutlinePath.markdownDescription: Name targets by their outline path (`Projects/Alpha/`). The three names start the path with the file, and offer the file itself, for its top level. (`org-refile-use-outline-path`)

reverseNoteOrder.markdownDescription: A refiled entry goes first under its target, not last. (`org-reverse-note-order`)

key.description: The keys that pick the template

prepend.description: First under the target, not last

target.description: `file` and a path; `file+headline`, a path and a headline; or `file+olp`, a path and the headlines of an outline path

type.description: An Org entry (the default), or plain text

captureTemplates.markdownDescription: Capture templates. Each has a `key`, a `description`, a `type` (`entry`, the default, or `plain`), a `target` and a `template` (text, or a list of lines), and may have `prepend`, `emptyLines`, `emptyLinesBefore`, `emptyLinesAfter` and `immediateFinish`. The target is a list: `file` and a path; `file+headline`, a path and a headline; or `file+olp`, a path and the headlines of an outline path. An empty path is `defaultNotesFile`, and without a target the entry goes at the end of `defaultNotesFile`. A template with only a key and a description groups the templates whose keys start with its key. (`org-capture-templates`)

orgDirectory.markdownDescription: Where the relative paths of capture targets are. (`org-directory`)

defaultNotesFile.markdownDescription: The target of a capture template whose file is empty. (`org-default-notes-file`)

linkDescriptive.markdownDescription: Show a link as its description (or its target, when it has none) and hide the rest: the brackets, and the target of a link with a description. The text is marked `hidden` in the highlighting, and editors that can conceal text conceal it. (`org-link-descriptive`)

hideEmphasisMarkers.markdownDescription: Hide the markers around `*bold*`, `/italic/`, `_underline_`, `+strike-through+`, `=verbatim=` and `~code~`, as for links. (`org-hide-emphasis-markers`)

autoSave.markdownDescription: Save the files a command changes other than the one it was run in: an entry's file changed from the agenda, the target of a capture or of a refile. The editor saves them once it has made the change. Off, they are left with unsaved changes, as Emacs leaves them.

cycleSeparatorLines.markdownDescription: With at least this many blank lines after a subtree, the last one stays outside its fold. Negative: all of them stay outside. `0`: none does. (`org-cycle-separator-lines`)

adaptIndentation.markdownDescription: Indent the lines of an entry past its headline's stars: `true` for all of them, `"headline-data"` for the planning line, drawers and clock lines right below the headline. Applies to new lines, to re-indenting (range formatting) and to what commands write. (`org-adapt-indentation`)

srcPreserveIndentation.markdownDescription: Leave the code of source blocks as it is indented when re-indenting. (`org-src-preserve-indentation`)

editSrcContentIndentation.markdownDescription: How far code is indented past its source block when re-indenting. (`org-edit-src-content-indentation`)

span.markdownDescription: How much time the agenda shows. (`org-agenda-span`)

startOnWeekday.markdownDescription: The day a week or fortnight starts on; `false` starts it today. (`org-agenda-start-on-weekday`)

deadlineWarningDays.markdownDescription: How many days before a deadline it shows up. (`org-deadline-warning-days`)

scheduledDelayDays.markdownDescription: How many days after its date a scheduled entry shows up. (`org-scheduled-delay-days`)

scheduledPastDays.markdownDescription: How many days a scheduled entry that is not done keeps showing up. (`org-scheduled-past-days`)

deadlinePastDays.markdownDescription: How many days a missed deadline keeps showing up. (`org-deadline-past-days`)

skipScheduledIfDone.markdownDescription: Leave out scheduled entries that are done. (`org-agenda-skip-scheduled-if-done`)

skipDeadlineIfDone.markdownDescription: Leave out deadlines of entries that are done. (`org-agenda-skip-deadline-if-done`)

skipTimestampIfDone.markdownDescription: Leave out timestamps of entries that are done. (`org-agenda-skip-timestamp-if-done`)

showFutureRepeats.markdownDescription: Show the future dates of repeating entries: all of them, none, or only the next. (`org-agenda-show-future-repeats`)

tagsColumn.markdownDescription: Where tags are aligned in the agenda. Org's own default follows the window width, which a server does not know. (`org-agenda-tags-column`)

daily.markdownDescription: Draw the grid in a one-day agenda. (`org-agenda-time-grid`)

weekly.markdownDescription: Draw the grid for every day. (`org-agenda-time-grid`)

requireTimed.markdownDescription: Draw the grid only on days with an entry that has a time. (`org-agenda-time-grid`)

removeMatch.markdownDescription: Leave out grid lines at a time an entry already has. (`org-agenda-time-grid`)

times.markdownDescription: The times of the grid lines, as `800` for 8:00. (`org-agenda-time-grid`)

trailer.markdownDescription: What follows a time that has no end time. (`org-agenda-time-grid`)

line.markdownDescription: The text of a grid line. (`org-agenda-time-grid`)

now.markdownDescription: The text of the line for the current time. (`org-agenda-current-time-string`)

showCurrentTimeInGrid.markdownDescription: Show the current time in the grid. (`org-agenda-show-current-time-in-grid`)

weekendDays.markdownDescription: The days drawn as the weekend (0 is Sunday). (`org-agenda-weekend-days`)

startWithLogMode.markdownDescription: Start the agenda in log mode, which shows what was closed and clocked each day (`l` toggles it). (`org-agenda-start-with-log-mode`)

startWithClockreportMode.markdownDescription: Start the agenda with the clock report under it (`R` toggles it). (`org-agenda-start-with-clockreport-mode`)

logModeItems.markdownDescription: What log mode shows: `closed` entries, `clock` lines and `state` changes. (`org-agenda-log-mode-items`)

blockSeparator.markdownDescription: What goes between the blocks of a block agenda: one character repeated across 79 columns, a longer text as it is, or `false` for nothing. In a block's `settings`, the separator above that block. (`org-agenda-block-separator`)

compactBlocks.markdownDescription: Leave out the separators between blocks and the header over agenda blocks. (`org-agenda-compact-blocks`)

hideEmptyBlocks.markdownDescription: Leave out the blocks of a block agenda that show no entries. Not in Org.

startDay.markdownDescription: The day the agenda starts from, as the date prompt reads it: `-1d`, `+2d`, `2026-10-01`. (`org-agenda-start-day`)

blocks.description: Views shown one after the other

header.description: Replaces the view's header; empty for none

match.description: For todo, keywords; for tags, a match string

settings.description: Agenda options for this block: span, startDay…

header.description: Replaces the view's header; empty for none

key.description: The keys that pick the command in the agenda menu

match.description: For todo, keywords (NEXT|WAIT); for tags, a match string (work-home, PRIORITY="A")

settings.description: Agenda options for this command: span, startDay…

customCommands.markdownDescription: Commands of the agenda menu. Each has a `key` and a `description`, and either a `type` (`agenda`, `alltodo`, `todo`, `tags` or `tags-todo`) with a `match` (keywords such as `NEXT|WAIT` for `todo`, a match string such as `work-home` or `PRIORITY="A"` for `tags`), or `blocks`, a list of such views shown one after the other. `header` replaces a view's header (empty: none), and `settings` holds agenda options for the command or a block (`span`, `startDay`…). A command with only a key and a description groups the commands whose keys start with its key. (`org-agenda-custom-commands`)
